spec_match.rationale: Reads real LayoutShift entries with previousRect/currentRect, DPR, and viewport — the right surface — but the support probe labelled 'LayoutShift API' only tests 'PerformanceObserver' in window rather than supportedEntryTypes.includes('layout-shift'), and the CSS-px-vs-physical-px change itself is unobservable at DPR 1 with no simulated comparison on this page.

interactive.rationale: The only demo flow cannot populate its own readout: clicking Trigger shift moves the box within the 500ms input window, so the resulting entry has hadRecentInput=true and the observer's `if (entry.hadRecentInput) continue` discards it — verified via CDP (click left value/prevRect/currentRect at '—' while a parallel observer saw the entries with hadRecentInput:true).

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises triggering a shift and reading the entry's value, rects, and DPR — the right spec framing, even though the implementation currently defeats it.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles missing PerformanceObserver, but the central edge case — hadRecentInput on user-triggered shifts — is what breaks the page, and nothing explains it.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite (6/6 passing here) asserts interface/field existence — LayoutShift, LayoutShiftAttribution, prevRect/currentRect, devicePixelRatio — which is reasonable given the unit change is not directly observable, but it proves structure, not the CSS-pixel semantics.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Interaction was driven with real CDP clicks in headless Chromium 141: the box shifts, console stays clean, but the captured-entry panel never updates — the core output state could not be verified because the page filters out its own events.

telemetry_health.rationale: Server-injected /public/demo-telemetry.js verified in the served DOM.

design_system.rationale: Design-system variables throughout; stage, cards, and buttons follow the shared shell.

accessibility.rationale: Native labelled buttons, but all six info-row values update (or would) silently with no live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-measured clean at 360x740 (scrollWidth 360); desktop 1280 verified via screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Make the triggered shift observable — stop discarding hadRecentInput entries or trigger outside the input window
openQuestions.detail: Verified with CDP: clicking Trigger shift produces LayoutShift entries with hadRecentInput=true which the observer skips, so entry.value/previousRect/currentRect stay '—' forever — the probe can never return true. Either schedule the mutation >500ms after the click (with a visible countdown) so hadRecentInput is false, or display hadRecentInput entries explicitly labelled as input-adjacent. Also teach the page why (the hadRecentInput CLS exclusion) — it is the feature's most practical gotcha. Same defect exists on shift-reporter and zoom-resilience-checker; fix all three consistently.

openQuestions.title: Probe layout-shift support specifically
openQuestions.detail: Replace the 'PerformanceObserver' in window check behind the 'LayoutShift API' label with PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes.includes('layout-shift') so the label matches what is probed (rule: no broad baseline probes).

openQuestions.title: Announce captured entries via a live region
openQuestions.detail: The captured-entry rows change silently; add aria-live=polite to the info card once the readout actually works.

summary: Broken core flow: the page's own hadRecentInput filter discards every shift its Trigger button causes, so the captured-entry panel can never populate (CDP-verified: entries exist with hadRecentInput:true, readouts stay '—'). Page otherwise loads clean on both viewports and the structure/probe scaffolding is right; a small trigger-delay fix restores the whole demo. Browser-verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshot + DOM dump) and raw CDP (real click dispatch, console/network capture, 360x740 DPR3 mobile emulation) — chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session. Chromium 141 predates Chrome 145, so v145-only API paths were validated on their fallback branches, not the new-API success path. The single failed fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet request is environmental (blocked host) and was not counted against any page.
